limitations: Firefox file input uses a File/DataTransfer fixture, not the operating-system picker.
Browser/computer termination during the multi-API restore is not power-loss-atomic and was not fault-injected.
ZIP, encryption, cloud sync and third-party backup formats are outside this version.
review: Reused settings, metadata/value/dependency validators and existing transaction queues. Fixed narrow table layout and stale appearance replies.
Used compact JSON to preserve the backup budget for deeply nested valid GM values; reduced exported helpers and fixed file-retry/unload behavior.
correctedAttempts: The sandbox could not launch/clean up its isolated Chrome process. Reruns used the existing harness outside the sandbox; cleanup was restricted to the failed run's exact profile.
Native Chrome exposed narrow table header overflow; scoped wrapping and fixed table layout resolved it.
Firefox rejected statement-style test expressions; they were changed to expressions accepted by both adapters.
The navigation fixture expected four child documents; it now checks one document per visited section and only one visible child.
The broader page fixture also had a six-section menu expectation; its exact expected menu now includes Backup & restore. The full suite then passed 827 checks.
